image_description: A close-up view of the front wheel assembly of a white dirt bike. The image features a knobby off-road tire, a spoked wheel rim, and a prominent disk brake system. The brake rotor is a drilled metal disc with an orange mounting carrier. A black caliper is mounted to the fork leg. The suspension forks (black stanchions with silver lowers) are visible above the axle. The background consists of a concrete floor and a brown brick wall.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular, metallic, and its diameter significantly exceeds its thickness, consistent with a motorcycle disk brake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A black mechanical housing (caliper) is visible clamping onto the outer edge of the rotor, attached to the suspension fork.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This checkpoint describes an automotive hub interface. Motorcycle rotors typically mount via a carrier or directly to the hub face without external 'lug bolts' visible in this manner. The mounting hardware is obscured by the orange carrier/spider.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears to be a single-layer drilled disc (common for motorcycles), which falls under the 'solid' or simplified ventilated category acceptable for this class. It is not a solid slab; it has holes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are internal components housed within the caliper jaws. They are not externally visible in this standard exterior shot.
A black hydraulic hose is visible running along the fork leg and connecting towards the caliper area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface clearly exhibits a pattern of cross-drilled holes, a common feature for heat dissipation in performance brakes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface appears clean and silver/metallic. There is no significant blueing or browning indicative of heavy heat cycling or wear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the matte, slightly textured finish typical of cast metal components used in automotive/motorcycle applications.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific mechanical identity of the braking assembly and distinguish it from generic wheels or other machinery.
To verify the spatial relationship between the fork, axle, rotor, and tire, ensuring no floating elements or depth bleeding.
To check the integrity of the thin metal disc edges and the drilled holes for any melting or structural collapse artifacts.
To assess overall texture consistency of the tire rubber, metal reflections, and background bricks.

focus_areas: Integrity of the drilled holes in the brake rotor (check for warping or filling).
Connection point of the hydraulic line to the caliper (check for fusion).
Spoke-to-rim connectivity (check for missing or floating spokes).
Tire tread texture consistency (check for smearing).
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'lug bolt pattern' checkpoint. The taxonomy prior knowledge seems biased toward automotive brakes. In this motorcycle context, the absence of automotive-style lug bolts is correct, not an artifact. Ensure the Reflector does not penalize the image for lacking automotive-specific features when the subject is clearly a motorcycle component. Verify if the 'heat discoloration' absence is a defect or simply indicates a new/clean part.
